channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank reports 34% annual growth in bank deposits
item.description: Bank deposits in Uzbekistan increased by 34% over the past year, according to the Central Bank. The regulator stated that this significant growth contributes to the expansion of financial resources, with the largest portion deposited for terms up to one year.

item.title: Uzbek President emphasizes unity and reforms amid global risks
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stressed the importance of national unity, appreciating peace, and accelerating reforms in the face of growing global threats. He highlighted that reforms are valued through labor and public satisfaction, linking internal changes with foreign policy efforts to find partners.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Silk Road Fund to Finance Infrastructure Projects with $395 Million
item.description: Uzbekistan's National Bank for Foreign Economic Activity and the Silk Road Fund signed an agreement to finance infrastructure projects in Uzbekistan for up to $395 million. The deal was reached during the 11th "Belt and Road" Summit in Hong Kong. The focus will be on modernizing transport infrastructure, including toll roads.

item.title: Uzbekistan imported least gasoline in August since start of year
item.description: Uzbekistan imported the least amount of gasoline in August compared to the beginning of the year. Fuel purchases from abroad decreased 7.8 times compared to January. The cost of gasoline imports significantly increased.

item.title: Russia Targets Truck Near NATO and Poland Border
item.description: Russia targeted a truck near the NATO and Poland border, approximately 800 meters from the Dorohusk–Yahodin crossing point. Moscow stated the strike was aimed at infrastructure used for transporting military cargo from Europe to Ukraine.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Cover Part of Business Loan Interest Rates
item.description: Uzbekistan will cover a portion of bank loan interest rates for entrepreneurs. The compensation will not consider credit history, business category, or stability rating. Interest-free lending for family entrepreneurship will increase.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Forge Special Strategic Partnership in Technology and Industry
item.description: Uzbekistan designates South Korea as a key partner for technological and industrial cooperation, elevating relations to a special strategic partnership. This move aligns with Uzbekistan's pragmatic foreign policy and aims to transform its geographic advantage into technological capital amidst global competition in advanced manufacturing.

item.title: Medvedev threatens to erase Lithuania from world map over nuclear weapons deployment
item.description: Dmitry Medvedev threatened to erase Lithuania from the world map, warning Vilnius of consequences for deploying nuclear weapons on its territory. He stated that NATO's Article 5 would not be practically applied against Russia.

item.title: BRICS Summit in New Delhi Focuses on Future Cooperation Amid Global Changes
item.description: The 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi is a platform for defining future cooperation and discussing international and regional agendas amidst global economic and security shifts. Chinese President Xi Jinping highlighted 20 years of BRICS cooperation, emphasizing peace, stability, innovation, and mutual understanding.

item.title: Experts urge Central Asia to enhance cybersecurity through data sharing and financial literacy
item.description: Experts recommend Central Asian countries prioritize continuous data exchange and improve citizens' financial literacy in cybersecurity. They advise abandoning outdated approaches for modern realities in developing protection mechanisms. This was discussed at the Silk Road Finance & Technology Forum in Tashkent.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Criminal Liability for Interfering with Judicial Proceedings
item.description: Uzbekistan's Criminal Code now penalizes officials who illegally influence judges to obstruct fair trials, issue unjust rulings, or secure specific decisions. Those found guilty face up to five years in prison.

item.title: Karalpakstan Officials Meet with German Cooperation Society (GIZ) Representatives
item.description: Officials from the Republic of Karalpakstan met with representatives from the German Society for International Cooperation (GIZ). Discussions focused on close partnership between Germany and Uzbekistan, reforms in Aral Sea region development, and joint projects in economy, ecology, medicine, and education.

item.title: Xi Jinping Calls for Expanded BRICS Cooperation and Global South Collaboration
item.description: At the BRICS summit in New Delhi, Chinese President Xi Jinping urged for enhanced cooperation and interaction among member states. He emphasized the growing importance of the Global South in shaping a multipolar world and proposed five initiatives for cooperation in AI, trade, digital economy, manufacturing, and human resources.

item.title: BRICS Summit in New Delhi: India and China's Role in a Transforming Multipolar World
item.description: The BRICS Summit in New Delhi is a significant moment for evolving a multipolar international order. The relationship between China and India, as major developing economies and voices of the Global South, influences global dynamics. BRICS provides a platform for dialogue, advancing common interests, and managing differences.

item.title: Xi Jinping attends BRICS summit in New Delhi, discusses global development
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping participated in the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi. He delivered a speech on "BRICS: A Responsible Vanguard in Global Development," highlighting 20 years of cooperation and the bloc's influence on emerging markets and developing countries. Xi emphasized BRICS' role in overcoming global challenges and supporting the Global South.

item.title: India's First Investment Project in Kyrgyzstan, Avelum Partner, Reaches Production Stage
item.description: The Solton-Sary gold recovery plant, India's first investment project in Kyrgyzstan from exploration to production, has launched in test mode. Avelum Partner LLC, a subsidiary of India's Deccan Gold Mines Ltd, partnered with Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC.

item.title: India's first investment project in Kyrgyzstan, Avelum Partner, reaches production
item.description: The Solton-Sary gold recovery plant has launched in test mode in Kyrgyzstan, marking a significant milestone. Avelum Partner, India's first investment project in the country to reach industrial production, is a subsidiary of Deccan Gold Mines Ltd. The project represents successful India-Kyrgyzstan investment cooperation.

item.title: Somoniyon School Operates Without a License After Expiration

item.title: Nearly 100,000 Uzbek Citizens Returned from Russia in 10 Days
item.description: Almost 100,000 Uzbek citizens returned to Uzbekistan from Russia between August 25 and September 5, according to the Migration Agency of Uzbekistan. Of these, 54,885 arrived directly, and 41,530 came via Kazakhstan. Assistance was provided to 5,467 individuals.

item.title: Nearly 100,000 Uzbek citizens returned from Russia in 10 days
item.description: Almost 100,000 Uzbek citizens returned to Uzbekistan from Russia within a 10-day period, according to the Migration Agency of Uzbekistan. Of these, over 54,000 arrived directly, and more than 41,000 came via Kazakhstan. Assistance was provided to over 5,400 citizens.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev begins state visit to South Korea
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and his wife have arrived in Seoul for a state visit. The agenda includes negotiations with President Lee Jae-myung, meetings with officials and business leaders, and participation in the Central Asia-South Korea summit.

item.title: Tajikistan's economy: A look back at 35 years of development since the 1990s crisis
item.description: This report examines the economic path of Tajikistan over the past 35 years, tracing its development from the crisis of the 1990s to its current economy with a GDP of hundreds of billions of somoni. Further details are available.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce Benefits for Mothers Returning to Work Before Child Turns One
item.description: Uzbekistan will implement a system providing benefits for women who return to work before their child reaches one year of age. This benefit will be paid from the State Social Insurance Fund and will take effect starting January 1, 2027. The measure aims to support working mothers.

item.title: Uzbekistan Needs Clear Rules for Drivers Yielding to Ambulances
item.description: Reports of drivers failing to yield to ambulances are frequent in Uzbekistan. While drivers are fined, the issue persists due to a lack of clear traffic rules. Current regulations only state that drivers must yield, but do not specify how to do so in various traffic situations, leading to disorganized passage for emergency vehicles.

item.title: Tajik Deputy Prime Minister Usmonali Usmonzoda turns 67, oversees energy sector
item.description: Tajik Deputy Prime Minister Usmonali Usmonzoda celebrated his 67th birthday. He has served in this role for six years, overseeing the energy sector. Usmonzoda previously served as Minister of Energy and Water Resources and Vice President of the CIS Electric Power Council. He has been involved in addressing electricity shortages and power grid issues.

item.title: Kushner comments on Moscow and Kyiv visits, seeking US-brokered Ukraine conflict resolution
item.description: Jared Kushner stated the US aims to facilitate a Ukraine conflict resolution acceptable to both Moscow and Kyiv. He identified territory as the most complex issue, with differing positions. Kushner noted that if Ukraine agreed to Russia's stated boundaries, other aspects could be settled. He emphasized the US role in finding a solution aligned with Ukraine's goals.

item.title: Kushner comments on Moscow and Kyiv visits, discusses Ukraine conflict resolution
item.description: Jared Kushner stated that the US aims to facilitate a resolution to the Ukraine conflict acceptable to both Moscow and Kyiv. He identified territory as the most challenging issue due to differing positions. Kushner noted that if Ukraine agreed to Russia's proposed borders, other aspects of a deal could be settled.

item.title: BRICS nations adopt joint declaration on nuclear threats, trade, and sanctions
item.description: BRICS leaders issued a joint declaration expressing concern over rising nuclear threats and conflicts. They called for cooperation to ensure global trade, supply chains, and energy function smoothly. The declaration also addressed concerns about unilateral trade measures and urged the cancellation of sanctions.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev arrives in Seoul for state visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, accompanied by his wife, arrived in Seoul for a state visit. He was greeted with a ceremonial welcome at the Korean Air Force base. Mirziyoyev later met with Uzbek citizens working and studying in Korea to discuss their plans and the country's ongoing reforms.

item.title: Iran sends seven conditions to US for reopening Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Tehran has conveyed seven conditions to Washington through intermediaries for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz for full navigation, according to Tasnim agency. The conditions have not been disclosed. The strait will remain closed until the US approves these demands, an informed source stated.

item.title: Lavrov: Russia will not stop fighting for negotiations
item.description: Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov responded to Ukrainian President's offer to meet Putin in Miami, stating that Russia will not halt its military operations for negotiations. The Kremlin assessed the proposal as "impossible."

item.title: Registration deadline extended for Kyrgyz citizens seeking work in South Korea
item.description: The registration period for Kyrgyz citizens wishing to work in South Korea has been extended. An additional online registration will open on September 14 until the required number of workers is reached, as part of the EPS program.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Political Developments: Presidential Election Set for January 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's parliament plans to consider a decree setting the presidential election for January 27, 2027, with campaigning to start in late December. Meanwhile, the Bishkek court reclassified the 'letter of 75' case from attempted power seizure to Article 195 of the Criminal Code, sentencing defendants to four years with a two-year probation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Political Landscape: Presidential Election Date Set, "Letter of 75" Case Concludes
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's political scene is heating up with plans to set the presidential election for January 27, 2027. Meanwhile, the "Letter of 75" case saw defendants reclassified from attempted power seizure to Article 195 of the Criminal Code, receiving four-year suspended sentences. Independence Day celebrations in Talas Oblast included opening infrastructure projects.

item.title: Uzbek President to Visit South Korea for State Visit and Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will undertake a state visit to South Korea from September 13-16 at the invitation of President Yoon Suk Yeol. Discussions will focus on strengthening strategic partnership, economic cooperation, and cultural exchanges. Mirziyoyev will also attend the first Central Asia-South Korea summit in Seoul.

item.title: Iran Used Chinese Satellite Imagery for Attack on US Base in Jordan
item.description: Iran reportedly utilized Chinese satellite imagery to target a US base in Jordan, causing damage to over 20 structures and resulting in three fatalities. Washington considers this the most credible evidence of US military casualties due to Chinese support.

item.title: Uzbekistan Condemns Attacks on Saudi Arabia, Urges Diplomatic Resolution
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed deep concern over missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia. The ministry strongly condemns any actions threatening civilian populations, infrastructure, and regional security. Uzbekistan supports UN and regional efforts to de-escalate tensions and establish lasting peace through political and diplomatic means.

item.title: Judicial Financing in Uzbekistan to Be Solely from State Budget
item.description: The financing of court activities in Uzbekistan will exclusively come from the state budget. The distribution of allocated funds for the Constitutional Court, Supreme Court, and the Supreme Judicial Council will be handled by these respective bodies. Other courts' funding will be managed by the Department for Ensuring Court Activities under the Supreme Court.

item.title: Parliaments of Uzbekistan and Lithuania to support mutually beneficial initiatives
item.description: A delegation from Uzbekistan's Oliy Majlis visited Lithuania for meetings with parliamentary groups on cooperation. Discussions focused on inter-parliamentary interaction, legislative improvement, regional development, environmental protection, and water resource management. Both sides agreed to strengthen cooperation and support mutually beneficial initiatives.

item.title: Uzbek President to visit South Korea for first Central Asia-Korea summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit South Korea on a state visit to attend the first Central Asia-Republic of Korea summit. Discussions will focus on cooperation in trade, investment, infrastructure, digital transformation, science, and technology.
